description: LLM observability platform — issues credentials in PAIRS: a public key (`pk-lf-...`) used as the basic-auth username and a secret key (`sk-lf-...`) used as the basic-auth password. Both must be present for the SDK to authenticate; rotating one without the other breaks ingest. Self-hosted Langfuse uses the same shapes; only the host URL changes.

variants.description: Pairs with the secret key for basic auth against `/api/public/*` endpoints. Safe to expose in client-side code (it identifies the project, does not authorise writes alone) but the framework still treats it as a secret because rotating it requires the matching secret-key rotation.

steps: Pick the project from the top-left switcher
Settings → API keys → Create new keys
Copy BOTH the public and secret key — the secret is shown once, the public can be re-fetched
retrieval.notes: Langfuse rotates the pair atomically — clicking Create generates a new (public, secret) tuple together. Update both env vars in lockstep when you rotate.

rotation.notes: Langfuse credentials rotate as a PAIR. Click Create new keys to mint a fresh (public, secret) tuple, update BOTH LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY and LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY in lockstep, then delete the old pair. The old pair keeps working until you delete it — that is your manual overlap window. Rotating only one half breaks ingest with a 401.

variants.description: Pairs with the public key for basic auth. Treat as a real password — leaking it lets anyone write to your Langfuse project's traces.

steps: Pick the project from the top-left switcher
Settings → API keys → Create new keys
Copy BOTH the public and secret key — the secret is shown once and CANNOT be recovered
retrieval.notes: Lost secret keys cannot be re-displayed — you must rotate (which generates a new pair, invalidating the old public key too). Ingest stops until both new keys land in the consumer.

rotation.notes: The secret key rotates only as part of the (public, secret) pair — see the public-key variant for the full procedure. Never rotate the secret alone: the matching public key is invalidated at the same time, so a half-rotation is a guaranteed 401.
